[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance addresses the gap between architecture decisions (ADRs) and their implementation in code. ADRs document *what* was decided and *why*, but they rarely express decisions in terms that are directly actionable by developers or AI agents. This guidance defines an approach for extracting verifiable implementation constraints from ADRs — bridging the gap so that decisions are not merely documented but actively enforced during implementation.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Decisions translate to code**: Architecture decisions are enforced through concrete constraints rather than relying on developer memory or tribal knowledge
- **Verification is explicit**: Each constraint carries a verification method (test, lint, structural check) — reviewers and CI pipelines can confirm compliance
- **Agent execution quality**: When agent task specs reference decision-derived constraints, agents produce output that respects architectural intent without requiring the agent to interpret full ADR documents
- **Audit trail from decision to deployment**: Every constraint traces to its source ADR, creating a verifiable chain from decision rationale to implemented behavior
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

- **Primary**: Architects who author ADRs and need to ensure their decisions are implementable and verifiable
- **Secondary**: Engineers who implement features governed by ADRs and need to understand what constraints apply
- **Tertiary**: Spec authors who need to populate the "Project Architecture Decisions" category (Category 2) of the constraint taxonomy ([GUID-GOV-IMPL-006](../../governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-006-constraint-source-taxonomy-for-agent-task-specs.md))
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#applicable-scenarios]

#### Applicable Scenarios

- A project has one or more ADRs and needs to ensure they are respected during implementation
- An architect is authoring a new ADR and wants to define its verifiable constraints at decision time
- A team is adopting AI agent execution and needs to bridge their ADRs into agent-consumable constraints
- A project is conducting an architecture health check and needs to verify ADR compliance

[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#scope-boundaries]

#### Scope Boundaries

- **In Scope**: The process of extracting constraints from ADRs; classifying constraints by verification type; expressing constraints in implementation-ready form; integrating with agent task specifications
- **Out of Scope**: How to write ADRs (see the [ADR template](../../../../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/architecture-decision-record.md)); the spec authoring process itself ([GUID-GOV-IMPL-003](../../governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md)); CI pipeline implementation details
- **Related Guidance**: [GUID-GOV-IMPL-006](../../governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-006-constraint-source-taxonomy-for-agent-task-specs.md) — taxonomy Category 2 consumes the constraints this guidance produces

page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#business-drivers]

#### Business Drivers

Architecture decisions represent significant organizational investment — they involve research, evaluation, stakeholder alignment, and formal approval. Yet in practice, many decisions degrade over time because there is no mechanism to ensure they are respected during daily development work. The decision exists in a document; the code evolves without reference to it.

This guidance addresses the "decision-implementation gap" — the distance between a documented ADR and its manifestation in running systems. Closing this gap means:

- Decisions produce measurable outcomes (not just documentation)
- Violations are caught at implementation time (not during post-hoc audits)
- Architecture governance operates continuously (not periodically)
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#strategic-alignment]

#### Strategic Alignment

This guidance supports the enterprise strategy of **architecture as code** — treating architectural decisions as executable constraints that are verified by automated systems, not just reviewed by humans.
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#the-decision-implementation-gap]

#### The Decision-Implementation Gap

```
                    The Gap
                ◄──────────►
ADR-007: "Use Redis for    ←→    Implementation uses Memcached
session caching"                  because the developer didn't
                                  read ADR-007
```

ADRs are written in natural language for human comprehension. They explain context, evaluate options, and justify choices. This format is essential for the *decision-making* audience but is poorly suited for the *implementation* audience. Developers need:

- Concrete constraints ("use Redis, not Memcached")
- Specific verification methods ("test that the session store configuration resolves to Redis")
- Clear scope boundaries ("applies to all session-handling services")
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#constraint-as-a-bridge-concept]

#### Constraint as a Bridge Concept

A **constraint** bridges the gap between an ADR and implementation. It is a statement that:

1. **Derives from** a specific ADR (traceable)
2. **Applies to** a specific scope of code or configuration (bounded)
3. **Can be verified** by an automated or manual check (testable)

Constraints are not ADRs themselves — they are the *implementation-facing projection* of an ADR. One ADR may produce zero constraints (if it's purely informational) or many constraints (if it governs multiple aspects of implementation).
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Most organizations have one of three dysfunctional states:

1. **ADRs exist but have no implementation teeth**: Decisions are documented but never referenced during coding, reviews, or CI. They are historical records, not active governance.

2. **ADRs are silently violated**: A developer (or agent) makes a choice that contradicts an ADR because the ADR's implications were never expressed in terms the developer encounters during their workflow.

3. **ADR compliance is checked only during manual reviews**: An architect periodically audits the codebase against decisions. Violations are found weeks or months after introduction, making remediation expensive.
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#impact-assessment]

#### Impact Assessment

- Architecture governance is reactive rather than proactive
- Decisions degrade over time as the codebase evolves without reference to them
- Agent-executed tasks cannot reference ADR intent unless constraints are explicitly extracted and included in specs
- Code review quality depends on the reviewer knowing all relevant ADRs from memory

page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#principle-1-every-adr-should-declare-its-verification-strategy]

#### Principle 1: Every ADR Should Declare Its Verification Strategy

**Description**: At the time an ADR is written (or during a subsequent extraction pass), the author should identify what verification type applies to each implementable aspect of the decision.

**Rationale**: If you cannot describe how to verify a decision is being followed, the decision is advisory rather than governance. Making the verification strategy explicit at authoring time forces clarity about what "compliance" means.

**Application**: Add a "Verification Strategy" section to each ADR (or maintain a separate constraint registry that references ADRs).
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#principle-2-constraints-are-derived-not-invented]

#### Principle 2: Constraints Are Derived, Not Invented

**Description**: Constraints are extracted from ADR text — they represent what the ADR already implies, expressed in a form suitable for implementation. They do not add new requirements beyond what the ADR decided.

**Rationale**: If a constraint goes beyond the ADR's decision, it should be its own ADR. Constraints are a projection, not an expansion.

**Application**: Each constraint must cite the specific ADR section or statement it derives from. If you cannot point to the source text, the constraint does not belong.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#principle-3-verification-types-determine-enforcement-mechanisms]

#### Principle 3: Verification Types Determine Enforcement Mechanisms

**Description**: Constraints are classified by how they can be verified, and this classification determines where enforcement happens in the development workflow.

**Rationale**: A constraint verified by a unit test operates differently from one verified by a structural check or a manual review. Knowing the verification type tells teams where to place enforcement.

**Application**: Use the verification type taxonomy (below) to classify each constraint and wire it to the appropriate enforcement mechanism.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#verification-type-taxonomy]

### Verification Type Taxonomy

Every constraint derived from an ADR falls into one of four verification types:

| Verification Type | What It Checks | Enforcement Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Behavioral** | The system exhibits specific runtime behavior | BDD scenarios, integration tests, contract tests | "Cache entries expire after the TTL specified in ADR-007" |
| **Structural** | The codebase has a specific shape or organization | Linters, architecture fitness functions, dependency checks | "No service imports from the Eligibility context (ADR-003 boundary)" |
| **Systemic** | A cross-cutting quality attribute is maintained | Load tests, security scans, observability checks | "All API endpoints respond within 200ms at P95 (ADR-011)" |
| **Configuration** | Infrastructure or runtime configuration is correct | Terraform plan validation, config schema checks, environment assertions | "Session store backend is Redis, not in-memory (ADR-007)" |
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#step-1-identify-implementable-statements-in-the-adr]

#### Step 1: Identify Implementable Statements in the ADR

Read the ADR's Decision section and Consequences section. For each statement, ask: *does this constrain what code or configuration should look like?*

**Yields constraints**:
- "We will use Redis for session caching" → constraint on technology choice
- "Services must not share databases" → constraint on data access patterns
- "All APIs must return structured error envelopes" → constraint on response format

**Does not yield constraints** (context/rationale only):
- "We evaluated Memcached but found it lacked TTL precision" → context, not constraint
- "This decision aligns with our cloud-native strategy" → justification, not constraint
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#step-2-express-each-constraint-in-implementation-ready-form]

#### Step 2: Express Each Constraint in Implementation-Ready Form

Transform the ADR statement into a concrete, verifiable constraint:

| ADR Statement | Constraint (Implementation-Ready) | Verification Type |
|---|---|---|
| "Use Redis for session caching" | Session store configuration must resolve to a Redis endpoint; no in-memory or Memcached backends in production configuration | Configuration |
| "Services must not share databases" | No service's data access layer may connect to a database owned by another bounded context; cross-context data access must use published APIs or events | Structural |
| "All APIs return structured error envelopes" | HTTP error responses (4xx, 5xx) must use the envelope format defined in STD-APP-API-001 §4.2; raw exception messages must not appear in response bodies | Behavioral |
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#step-3-assign-scope]

#### Step 3: Assign Scope

Each constraint applies to a defined scope — not necessarily the entire codebase:

```markdown
Constraint: Session store configuration must resolve to a Redis endpoint
Scope: All services in the Authentication bounded context
Source: ADR-007 § Decision
Verification: Configuration — environment variable CACHE_BACKEND must equal "redis"
```
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#step-4-record-the-constraint]

#### Step 4: Record the Constraint

Constraints can be recorded in any of these locations (choose based on team workflow):

| Storage Approach | Best For | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **Verification Strategy section in the ADR** | Small projects; keeps decisions and constraints co-located | Constraints are scattered across ADR files |
| **Dedicated constraint registry** (e.g., `docs/design/tech-specs.md`) | Large projects with many ADRs; provides a single queryable index | Requires cross-referencing between ADRs and registry |
| **Tagged in the traceability matrix** | Projects using formal traceability; connects requirements ↔ decisions ↔ tests | Higher overhead but maximum auditability |
| **Inline in agent task specs** | Agent-first workflows; constraints are expressed at the point of consumption | Constraints must be repeated across specs (or composed from a central reference) |

No single approach is mandated. The key requirement is that constraints are **written down, traceable to their source ADR, and discoverable** by those who need them (developers, reviewers, agents).

page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#for-architects-authoring-constraints-at-decision-time]

### For Architects: Authoring Constraints at Decision Time

When writing a new ADR, include a Verification Strategy section:

```markdown
## Verification Strategy

| Constraint ID | Constraint | Verification Type | Scope | Verified By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-007-C1 | Session store must use Redis backend | Configuration | Authentication services | Environment config validation in CI |
| ADR-007-C2 | Cache entries must respect TTL (not persist indefinitely) | Behavioral | All cache consumers | BDD scenario @FR-CACHE-003 |
| ADR-007-C3 | No direct Redis client usage — all access through the CachePort interface | Structural | All services | Import analysis (no `redis` package import outside adapters/) |
```

This approach makes constraints a first-class output of the decision process rather than an afterthought.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#for-existing-adrs-extraction-pass]

### For Existing ADRs: Extraction Pass

For ADRs written before this guidance existed, perform an extraction pass:

1. Read each ADR's Decision and Consequences sections
2. Identify implementable statements (per Step 1 above)
3. Transform into constraints with verification types
4. Record in the team's chosen storage approach
5. Wire high-priority constraints into CI (behavioral → tests; structural → linters; configuration → plan validation)

This is a one-time activity per ADR. Schedule it as part of an architecture health check or when onboarding a concern that is governed by existing ADRs.
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#for-spec-authors-consuming-constraints-in-agent-task-specs]

### For Spec Authors: Consuming Constraints in Agent Task Specs

When populating Category 2 (Project Architecture Decisions) of the constraint taxonomy ([GUID-GOV-IMPL-006](../../governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-006-constraint-source-taxonomy-for-agent-task-specs.md)):

1. Identify which ADRs govern the concern being implemented
2. Check if those ADRs have extracted constraints (verification strategy section or constraint registry)
3. Include relevant constraints in the spec's `## Constraints` section, citing the ADR and constraint ID:

```markdown
## Constraints
- ADR-007-C1: Session store must use Redis backend; do not introduce alternative cache backends
- ADR-007-C3: All cache access must go through the CachePort interface; do not import redis-py directly
```

If the ADR does not have extracted constraints, perform a lightweight extraction (Steps 1–2 only) to identify the relevant constraints for the spec.

page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#decision-types-and-their-typical-constraints]

### Decision Types and Their Typical Constraints

| ADR Type | Typical Constraints Produced | Verification Types |
|---|---|---|
| Technology selection | Backend choice, client library, version pinning | Configuration, Structural |
| Integration approach | Protocol (REST/gRPC/events), contract format, retry policy | Behavioral, Configuration |
| Data ownership | Database boundaries, API-only access, event publishing | Structural |
| Security posture | Authentication method, token handling, encryption requirements | Behavioral, Configuration |
| Performance SLAs | Response time budgets, caching strategy, pagination limits | Systemic, Behavioral |
| Code organization | Module boundaries, layer separation, naming conventions | Structural |
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#when-an-adr-produces-zero-constraints]

### When an ADR Produces Zero Constraints

Some ADRs are purely informational or strategic — they document a direction without constraining implementation. Examples:

- "We will evaluate serverless architecture for batch processing" (future-looking, no current constraint)
- "We chose AWS over Azure for cloud hosting" (decision is at the infrastructure level, not application code level)

If an ADR produces zero implementation constraints, that's acceptable. Not every decision needs to be projected into code. The test is: *would violating this decision be detectable in a code change?* If not, it may be a strategic decision rather than an implementation-governing one.
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#constraint-granularity-too-coarse-vs-too-fine]

### Constraint Granularity: Too Coarse vs. Too Fine

| Granularity | Example | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| **Too coarse** | "Follow ADR-007" | Not actionable — what specifically does ADR-007 require of this code? |
| **Right level** | "All cache access must go through CachePort (ADR-007-C3); do not import redis-py outside of adapters/" | Specific, verifiable, scoped |
| **Too fine** | "Line 42 of cache_service.py must call self._port.get() not self._redis.get()" | Over-specified — constrains implementation method rather than architectural boundary |

page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#example-1-technology-selection-adr]

### Example 1: Technology Selection ADR

**ADR-012**: "We will use PostgreSQL (not DynamoDB) for the Claims data store because our query patterns require complex joins and transactions."

**Extracted Constraints**:

| ID | Constraint | Verification | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-012-C1 | Claims data access must use PostgreSQL-compatible SQL; no DynamoDB SDK calls | Structural — import analysis | `src/claims/data/` |
| ADR-012-C2 | Database connection strings must point to a PostgreSQL endpoint | Configuration — env var validation | Deployment configs |
| ADR-012-C3 | Claims queries requiring transactions must use explicit transaction blocks (not autocommit) | Behavioral — integration test | All claim write operations |

**Spec usage**:
```markdown
## Constraints
- ADR-012-C1: Claims data access uses PostgreSQL; do not introduce DynamoDB SDK
- ADR-012-C3: All write operations must be wrapped in explicit transactions
```
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#example-2-bounded-context-boundary-adr]

### Example 2: Bounded Context Boundary ADR

**ADR-003**: "The Claims and Eligibility contexts must not share a database. Cross-context data access must use published events."

**Extracted Constraints**:

| ID | Constraint | Verification | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-003-C1 | No Claims service may import from `src/eligibility/` or reference Eligibility database tables | Structural — import/dependency analysis | All Claims services |
| ADR-003-C2 | Cross-context data needs must be served by consuming published domain events | Behavioral — integration test verifies event consumption | Claims ↔ Eligibility integration points |
| ADR-003-C3 | No shared database schema may contain tables owned by both contexts | Configuration — schema ownership check | Database migrations |
page_texts.42:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#example-3-adr-without-pre-extracted-constraints-lightweight-extraction]

### Example 3: ADR Without Pre-Extracted Constraints (Lightweight Extraction)

An engineer is writing a spec for a task governed by an older ADR that lacks a Verification Strategy section.

**ADR-005** (legacy format): "Session data should be encrypted at rest. We selected AES-256-GCM for symmetric encryption of session payloads."

**Lightweight extraction** (Steps 1–2 only, performed inline during spec authoring):

```markdown
## Constraints
- Per ADR-005: Session payloads must be encrypted using AES-256-GCM before storage
- Per ADR-005: Encryption keys must not be hardcoded — read from environment/secrets manager
- Do not use weaker encryption algorithms (AES-128, DES, etc.) for session data
```

The engineer does not need to create a full verification strategy table — the inline extraction is sufficient for the spec.

page_texts.45:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

- Architects SHOULD include a Verification Strategy section in new ADRs
- Teams SHOULD perform an extraction pass on existing ADRs that govern active development
- Constraint extraction is NOT mandatory for ADRs that are purely strategic or informational
- When an agent task spec references an ADR, it SHOULD include specific extracted constraints rather than citing the ADR as a whole

page_texts.47:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#relationship-to-enterprise-decision-records]

### Relationship to Enterprise Decision Records

Enterprise-level ADRs (in `eap-ref-architecture/decisions/`) follow the same constraint extraction approach. Enterprise constraints flow into project-level specs through [GUID-GOV-IMPL-006](../../governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-006-constraint-source-taxonomy-for-agent-task-specs.md) Category 1 (Enterprise Architecture Artifacts).

```
Enterprise ADR ──► Enterprise Constraint ──► Category 1 in spec
Project ADR    ──► Project Constraint    ──► Category 2 in spec
```

Both levels use the same extraction process. The difference is scope: enterprise constraints apply across all projects; project constraints apply within a single codebase.
page_texts.48:
[strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-008-decision-to-implementation-constraint-binding-guidance.md#architecture-health-check-integration]

### Architecture Health Check Integration

A periodic architecture health check can use extracted constraints as a compliance checklist:

1. Enumerate all ADRs with verification strategies
2. For each constraint, run the specified verification
3. Report compliance/violations
4. Prioritize remediation of violated constraints

This transforms architecture governance from "read the ADRs and hope" to "run the verification suite and know."

### Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| ADRs with verification strategies | ≥ 80% of active ADRs | Count ADRs with Verification Strategy section |
| Constraint coverage in specs | ≥ 1 Category 2 constraint per spec implementing an ADR-governed concern | Audit spec constraints against relevant ADRs |
| ADR violation detection rate | ≥ 90% caught at PR time (not post-deployment) | Track violations found in review vs. production incidents |
| First-run agent compliance | Agents respect ADR constraints on first attempt | Measure rework rate due to ADR violations in agent PRs |
